opportunities.title: Corrections Grade Tablets & Educational Software
opportunities.description: The County of San Mateo, Probation Department (the “County” and/or “Probation”) supports justice-involved youth by providing the mentorship and tools they need to succeed after detention. To enhance these efforts, we are seeking corrections-grade, tamper-resistant, rehabilitative tablets—secure mobile devices specifically designed to give detained youth access to vital educational and vocational resources. These tablets serve as a critical bridge for academic and vocational advancement, providing specialized preprogrammed software while maintaining essential family connectivity through strictly monitored, secure communication channels. Continuous oversight by Youth Services Center-Juvenile Hall (YSC-JH) staff ensures all interactions remain safe, appropriate and compliant with security protocols. In addition to supporting academic vocational and familial goals, the integration of vetted media – including movies and games - shall serve as key behavioral incentive to foster positive engagement and personal accountability. This comprehensive strategy reinforces vital support networks and cultivates the stability necessary for a successful reintegration into the community. The Probation Department is soliciting proposals from qualified vendors to deliver a comprehensive, secure and correction-grade tablet solution. The plan serves as a vital link between educational success, vocational growth and essential family support systems. The selected system must feature tamper-resistant hardware and pre-programmed, secure software for learning and monitored communication. By integrating strictly controlled family connectivity and vetted media (movies/games) as behavioral incentives, this initiative aims to maintain institutional security while providing youth with the digital tools and support networks essential for community reentry. This request seeks 50 units to achieve a 1-to-1 tablet-to-youth ratio allowing all youth to pursue a robust selection of courses like mathematics and resume writing, behavioral therapy and financial literacy modules. Additionally, the solution must facilitate the acquisition of trade-specific credentials and English as a Second Language (ESL) certifications to support career readiness and successful reentry. Furthermore, the selected vendor is required to provide initial on-site training and on-demand support for the duration of the contract. Additionally, a Dedicated Account Manager (DAM) shall be assigned to the Probation Department to facilitate regular progress meetings and ensure consistent ongoing assistance.

opportunities.title: Message Switch System Replacement
opportunities.description: The County of San Mateo (County) is seeking proposals from qualified vendors to replace its legacy Message Switch System (MSS), a mission-critical public safety platform that enables secure, real-time exchange of criminal justice information between local, state, and federal law enforcement systems. The Public Safety Communications (PSC) Department serves as the County's centralized emergency communications hub, providing 24/7 dispatch and emergency communication services for fire, emergency medical services (EMS), and law enforcement agencies serving approximately 800,000 residents throughout the County. The County's existing MSS supports approximately 30 law enforcement, public safety, and criminal justice agencies by providing secure connectivity to critical systems, including the California Law Enforcement Telecommunications System (CLETS), National Crime Information Center (NCIC), Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV), Automated Warrant System (AWS), County CJIS, and other criminal justice information systems. As the current platform has reached the end of its practical lifecycle, the County is seeking a modern, secure, scalable, and CJIS-compliant replacement that meets current operational needs while supporting regulatory compliance, interoperability, and future technology integration. The proposed solution will enhance system reliability, ensure uninterrupted access to critical criminal justice information, strengthen cybersecurity, and provide a sustainable platform that supports the County's long-term public safety mission.

opportunities.title: Wood Pole Inspection, Treatment, Repair, and UAV Inspection Services
opportunities.description: The City of Pasadena Water and Power Department (“PWP”) is seeking proposals from qualified and experienced firms to provide wood pole inspection, repair, restoration, treatment, and related reporting services for PWP’s electric distribution system. The selected firm will support PWP’s ongoing maintenance and compliance program for wood poles, including visual inspections, intrusive inspections, groundline inspections, preservative treatments, minor corrective repairs, pole reinforcement recommendations, installation of approved repair materials, and detailed reporting of observed conditions. PWP’s wood pole program is intended to support safe, reliable, and compliant operation of the electric distribution system in accordance with applicable requirements, including California Public Utilities Commission (“CPUC”) General Order 95, Rules for Overhead Electric Line Construction, and CPUC General Order 165, Inspection Requirements for Electric Distribution and Transmission Facilities. PWP’s system includes approximately 11,000 wood poles, including both municipally owned and jointly owned poles. A significant portion of the pole population is located in rear property or otherwise constrained access locations. The scope of services may include, but is not limited to, pole condition assessment, identification of structural damage or decay, inspection for General Order 95 infractions, groundline and below-ground inspections, preservative and fumigant treatment, installation of visibility strips, guy guards, ground molding, pole tags, and steel truss reinforcement where approved by PWP. The selected firm shall also provide detailed inspection records, photographs, condition ratings, repair recommendations, and electronic data deliverables in a format acceptable to PWP. In addition to conventional field inspection and treatment services, PWP intends to include drone or other unmanned aerial vehicle (“UAV”) inspection services under the resulting contract. UAV services may be used to supplement field inspections, improve access to difficult or hazardous locations, document pole-top conditions, capture high-resolution imagery, and support more efficient assessment of pole attachments, crossarms, hardware, conductors, insulators, and other visible overhead facilities. UAV services shall be performed by qualified, FAA-compliant personnel and in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements. The selected firm shall furnish all supervision, labor, materials, equipment, vehicles, tools, technology, software, transportation, permits, methods, processes, and incidentals necessary to complete the work in accordance with the final scope of services, applicable laws and regulations, industry standards, and PWP requirements.

opportunities.title: Fire and Life Safety Services
opportunities.description: The San Mateo County Sheriff’s Office is seeking qualified vendors to provide comprehensive Fire and Life Safety Services for its two correctional facilities. This project is intended to strengthen and modernize existing fire and life safety programs by ensuring full regulatory compliance, improving system reliability, and enhancing staff readiness in emergency situations. The selected vendor will play a critical role in supporting life safety operations within a secure custodial environment, where compliance with Board of State and Community Corrections (BSCC) standards and Cal/OSHA requirements is essential. In addition to performing inspections and audits, the vendor will help refine internal processes, update documentation and emergency planning, and assist in developing a long-term, sustainable approach to equipment maintenance and replacement. This effort is not limited to routine compliance checks; it is an opportunity to partner with the Sheriff’s Office to proactively identify gaps, implement best practices, and enhance coordination with local fire authorities. The County is seeking a vendor that brings both technical expertise and a collaborative approach to ensure that fire and life safety systems, equipment, and training programs are effective, current, and aligned with operational needs.

opportunities.title: Liability Claims Adjusting Services RFP
opportunities.description: General work description: The Request for Proposal (RFP) seeks a qualified Third-Party Administrator (TPA) to provide comprehensive liability claims adjusting and administration services for the County of Sacramento's self-insured liability program. The selected contractor will work collaboratively with County Risk Management personnel to investigate, evaluate, negotiate, defend, settle, and resolve liability claims while ensuring timely reporting, cost-effective claim management, and compliance with County requirements, the Public Risk Innovation, Solutions, and Management (PRISM) Liability Claims Administration Standards, and applicable laws and regulations. The contractor will also provide strategic recommendations, maintain proactive communication, and support the County's objective of minimizing claim costs and liability exposure. The scope of work includes end-to-end administration of existing and new liability claims, including prompt investigations, reserve analysis, litigation management, settlement negotiations, payment processing, subrogation and recovery efforts, legal administration, claims reporting, records management, and financial oversight. The contractor will maintain a secure claims management information system, provide County staff with access to claims data, coordinate with defense counsel and subject matter experts, support regulatory and Medicare reporting requirements, prepare annual claims reports for the Board of Supervisors, and participate in regular meetings with County staff to review claim strategies, identify trends, and recommend loss prevention initiatives. The contractor must also provide rapid local response capabilities for significant incidents and ensure continuity throughout contract transitions. The successful proposer will demonstrate extensive experience administering liability claims for California public entities, particularly those involving public entity exposures such as law enforcement, employment practices, civil rights, and medical malpractice. Emphasis will be placed on the firm's technical qualifications, claims management processes, reporting capabilities, staffing, local support, financial controls, and overall methodology for delivering efficient, responsive, and high-quality claims administration services that protect the County's interests and ensure compliance with established standards and contractual requirements.

opportunities.description: The County of Sacramento (County) is seeking proposals from qualified Community Based Organizations (CBOs) to partner with the County as Co-Applicant for the Extreme Heat Community Resilience Program (EHCRP) Round 2 grant, administered by the Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation (LCI). The selected CBO will work in partnership with PER team to develop and submit a competitive joint application for an Early Infrastructure Project and, if awarded, support implementation throughout the 30-month grant term. The County’s proposed project, Sacramento Beats the Heat: Cool 20 Infrastructure Plan (Cool 20 Plan), would pair a community cooling demonstration at Foothill Community Park with development of a broader infrastructure planning framework to identify, prioritize, and advance cost-effective cooling investments in County communities most vulnerable to extreme heat. The County is seeking a CBO partner with strong community relationships, demonstrated experience engaging vulnerable populations, and the capacity to lead meaningful community co-design and help translate community knowledge into implementable infrastructure solutions.

This will require actively participating in a national learning collaborative, including trainings, peer learning activities, and other implementation and continuous improvement efforts required by the Right at Home initiative. To implement the RAH program, the County expects to award contracts for the following roles: One (1) Legal Services Provider One (1) Network Coordinator / Fiscal Agent (on a separate RFP) Two- Four (2- 4 ) Supportive Service Providers (on a separate RFP) The County anticipates selecting one Legal Services Provider to deliver housing-related legal assistance to participants in the Right at Home (RAH) Targeted Homelessness Prevention Program. The Legal Services Provider will work collaboratively with the Network Coordinator/Fiscal Agent and Supportive Services Providers to help participants resolve legal issues that threaten housing stability and increase the risk of homelessness. opportunities.title: Establishment and Operation of Interim Housing for Families
opportunities.description: Through this Request for Information (RFI), the County of San Mateo (the County) Human Services Agency (HSA) Center on Homelessness (COH) seeks information from organizations that may be interested in establishing and/or operating an additional family interim housing program within San Mateo County Information gathered will assist the County in planning for expanded family interim housing capacity and a potential future solicitation for establishment and operation of one additional family interim housing program. This RFI is issued for information-gathering purposes only. No funds or contracts can or will be awarded through this RFI. This RFI is part of a market research effort to assess provider interest and capacity to add one family interim housing program in San Mateo County. The County is particularly interested in understanding: Whether qualified organizations are interested in operating a new family interim housing program; Whether qualified organizations are interested in procuring, leasing, acquiring, rehabilitating, developing, and/or constructing a facility for that purpose, including whether any already have a potential site in mind; Whether organizations would prefer to perform both the facility and operating roles, or perform one and partner with another organization; What supports, partnerships, or County involvement may be needed to make a project feasible. Information gathered through this process may inform program design, procurement strategy, service expectations, and a potential future Request for Proposals (RFP) or other solicitation. This RFI provides background on the County’s existing family shelter system, the need for additional family shelter capacity, and considerations for adding another family shelter program. Responses to this RFI are for informational and planning purposes only and do not obligate respondents to participate in any future procurement or take any other action. The County, through HSA’s COH, coordinates the homeless crisis response system. The system is designed to help individuals and families experiencing homelessness move toward stable housing. COH works countywide and collaborates with community-based organizations, public agencies, housing providers, and other stakeholders to strengthen the local homelessness response system. Family interim housing services are intended for households with children who are experiencing homelessness or a housing crisis and have no safe alternative housing options. In San Mateo County, these programs function as short-term, housing-focused interventions designed to provide a safe, decent, and family-appropriate place to stay while families stabilize, address immediate crises, and move as quickly as possible toward permanent housing. The County has not identified a specific region or facility for a new interim housing site. The County is seeking information from community-based organizations, shelter operators, housing and service providers, and other qualified entities with experience developing, establishing, and/or operating shelters or interim housing for families experiencing homelessness. The County is particularly interested in learning about provider capacity and considerations related to facility procurement and the provision of services relevant to adding another family shelter program to the County’s current system.

opportunities.title: Psychiatry Services at Sacramento County's Youth Detention Facility Open Enrollment
opportunities.description: Sacramento County Department of Health Services (DHS), Behavioral Health Services (BHS), is conducting an Open Enrollment to identify qualified individuals and organizations to provide psychiatric services for youth and young adults detained within Sacramento County’s Youth Detention Facility (YDF). The purpose of this Open Enrollment is to identify and contract with qualified psychiatrists to support County obligations under Title 15 of the California Code of Regulations, commencing with Article 8, Section 1400, Responsibility for Health Care Services (see Attachment A, Title 15 Minimum Standards for Juvenile Facilities). Psychiatry services under this Open Enrollment may include psychiatric assessment, diagnosis, and treatment; prescribing of psychotropic medications; medication evaluation, management, and monitoring; and consultation with YDF health and program staff. Services must be delivered safely, in a clinically appropriate manner, and in coordination with YDF multidisciplinary staff. Dispensing and administration of medications remains the responsibility of YDF health staff. Qualified providers are licensed physicians (M.D. or D.O.) who hold a current, active California medical license with board certification in psychiatry, and who are authorized to practice within the full scope of psychiatric medicine, including diagnosis and prescribing. Providers must be Board-Certified Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist, or board-eligible in child and adolescent psychiatry and actively pursuing board certification resulting in board-certification within 1 year of eligibility. Providers may contract individually or through a qualifying medical group or organization. All providers must adhere to applicable California laws, regulations, and professional standards of care. Contractors are required to comply with all regulatory requirements, facility policies and procedures, and expectations for coordination with YDF leadership and oversight entities. Applicants must meet all stated Minimum Qualifications (MQs) to be eligible for contract consideration with DHS. Contracts may be executed on a rolling basis based on County need and must be fully executed before the delivery of services or submission of invoices. Approval through this Open Enrollment does not guarantee referral volume or funding. County funding is limited to reimbursement for approved direct service costs only. This Open Enrollment will remain posted through July 1, 2028; however, the County reserves the right to close the posting earlier if the program capacity is reached.
